A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ensemble-watermark study. The main texts, algorithms, equations, tables and image-based appendix plots support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original watermark-detection, perplexity, paraphrasing-attack and text-length experiments in Section 4 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds feature-specific detector p-values in appendix Table 3.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 retain the same hash-derived keys, acrostic/sensorimotor/red-green logit adjustments and probability-product detector. The revisions do not change generation or detection procedures.

E1.justification: Both use C4 RealNewsLike for generation/detection, paraphrasing attacks and shortened-text evaluation. The new multilingual discussion introduces no actually evaluated language, dataset or task.

E2.justification: Both evaluate human text and the same seven watermark configurations, including red-green alone. New Table 3 reuses this configuration set without adding comparison methods.

E3.justification: The models, watermark weights, reported 400/300 sample counts, detection threshold, T5 replacement procedure and incremental sentence shortening remain unchanged. Table 3 reports existing-setting outputs without documenting a new evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: New Table 3 provides a component-level diagnostic, reporting each feature detector’s response across watermark configurations for medium-strength Llama 8B. Existing strength/perplexity, paraphrasing and text-length analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The existing significance threshold and Bonferroni-corrected Mann-Whitney analysis are retained, without new seed counts, repeated-run information or uncertainty intervals. Table 3 adds detector p-value outputs rather than a new uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: Table 3 adds 24 component p-values; the All Three row reports 0.00002030, 0.00022102 and 0.00000001 for sensorimotor, acrostic and red-green respectively. Existing detection rates, pairwise significance results, plotted trends and appendix results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The hashing equations, binomial-tail probabilities, red-green Z-score calculation and independence assumption for multiplying component probabilities are unchanged. No new formal derivation or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The ensemble contribution, shared detector, robustness claims and headline detection rates are retained. v2 explicitly identifies the 49% baseline as post-paraphrasing, matching the condition already established by v1’s evaluation.

C2.justification: New Section 6 substantially expands applicability and limitations: English-only implementation, alphabet restrictions for acrostics, sensorimotor-resource requirements and sequential generation with accessible logits. It also discusses model-specific keys for source attribution; v1 lacks this dedicated treatment.

D1.justification: The Introduction adds a GitHub link and states that all code and generated data are available. v1 provides no corresponding access statement; the implementation and hyperparameter descriptions otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Connell et al. (2012) to support its language-applicability discussion. Existing watermark positioning, including the distinction from Duwak, remains; publication-metadata updates and consolidation of duplicate Stamatatos references do not introduce different works.

P1.justification: Much of the Introduction and Background & Related Work is rewritten, with additional method/conclusion edits and a new Section 6. This is extensive editorial revision, although it also introduces duplicated wording and a missing title in the Devlin et al. reference.

P2.justification: The single-column preprint becomes a two-column document, extensively repositioning figures, tables and algorithms. Main figures are largely converted to vector graphics, Figure 2’s legends change, and the appendix adds Table 3 while relocating the old acrostic Table 3 as Table 4.

improvement.justification: The new limitations section and code/data access information improve transparency, while Table 3 adds useful component diagnostics. Core experimental validation remains unchanged. These limited gains outweigh localized editorial regressions, including the missing BERT reference title.
